entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
John de la Pole, 1st Earl of Lincoln, was a prominent figure in the Yorkist aristocracy during the Wars of the Roses.

He was born around 1436, and his family played a significant role in the power struggles of the time.

De la Pole's influence extended beyond England, as he was involved in the French and Italian courts, where he interacted with powerful figures like King Louis XI of France.

His legacy as a military leader and politician was cemented through his victories at the Battle of Barnet in 1471 and his involvement in the Battle of Tewkesbury in 1471.

As the Earl of Lincoln, de la Pole played a crucial role in the governance of the Earldom, overseeing its administration and collecting taxes.

Despite his influence, de la Pole's life was cut short when he died in 1487, at the age of around 51, in the Tower of London.

His death marked the end of an era, as the Yorkist claims to the throne ultimately failed.

The Earl's legacy can be seen in the continued influence of the Yorkist dynasty, which played a significant role in shaping English history for centuries to come.

John de la Pole's life serves as a reminder of the complex web of alliances and rivalries that characterized the Wars of the Roses, a period marked by violence, power struggles, and the eventual rise of the Tudor dynasty.
